supported: Within the matched 33 gulls, stronger flight-day individual ID gain did not consistently correspond to stronger low-speed individual ID gain; observed rho=0.102 with broad interval and p=0.5672.
Cross-day ID-associated centered altitude shape signal is present in both flight proxy and low-speed proxy at their respective spatial supports.
Measurement/device effects and microperch fidelity remain plausible alternatives.
not_supported: Flight ID shape is wholly explained by stable tag noise.
Absence of cross-context rank correlation rules out instrument confounding; flight-dependent sensor errors remain possible.
The individual identity signal demonstrates adaptive foraging or behavioral specialization.
Per-fix altitude logscore contrasts across different contexts/grids represent the same biological effect scale.
The study identifies a universal law shared with penguin breeding-component concentration.
methodological_caveats: Matched association is post-outcome exploratory, not independent replication.
Bird ID and tag ID are one-to-one during 2021; without re-tag or independent measurement, causes cannot be disentangled.
Flight and low-speed estimators condition on different horizontal grains (5000m versus100m).
Low-speed does not prove physical stationarity or identical perch elevation.
The exact-date label permutation changes the null-eligible-bird set; treat permutation exchangeability as an assumption.
Both flight and stationary per-bird gains show positive descriptive relationships with their own number of scored days.

next_boundary: Do not repeatedly re-score this same source to select a favorable explanation. Prefer independent device-calibrated altitude source or externally validated behavioral-state / wind context and a new frozen ecological test.
